title: Check: autoscaling
description: Five questions on scaling replicas from metrics.

questions.prompt: What must be running before an HPA on CPU can work?
questions.explanation: The HPA reads the metrics API, which metrics-server serves. Without it the HPA shows <unknown> for the current metric.

questions.prompt: An HPA targets 50% CPU. What is that a percentage of?
questions.explanation: Utilisation is measured against the request, which is why an HPA on a Pod with no CPU request cannot compute a target.

questions.prompt: Write the command that autoscales a Deployment named web between 2 and 10 replicas at 80% CPU.
questions.explanation: Fast to type and easy to edit afterwards - a good exam habit.

questions.prompt: You also set `replicas: 3` in the Deployment while an HPA manages it. What happens?

options.text: They fight - the HPA keeps overwriting the replica count
The API server rejects the HPA

questions.explanation: Two controllers writing the same field is a loop. Once an HPA owns a workload, stop setting replicas by hand.

questions.prompt: Why does an HPA scale down more slowly than it scales up?

options.text: A stabilisation window smooths out brief dips to avoid flapping
It does not - both are equally fast

questions.explanation: The default stabilisation window is five minutes down and zero up: react fast to load, retreat slowly.
